title: When more than one person owns the car
text: If two or more people are listed as owners, every owner has to sign the sale documents. The easiest way is for all owners to come to the appraisal appointment with their photo IDs. If an owner can't come, they can sign a power of attorney, form NW-POA-1, which must be notarized. Names joined by 'and' on the title need every owner to sign; names joined by 'or' need only one.

title: When more than one person owns the car
text: If two or more people are listed as owners, every owner has to sign the sale documents. The easiest way is for all owners to come to the appointment with their photo IDs. If an owner can't come, they can sign power of attorney form NW-POA-2, which can be signed electronically, with no notary. In Georgia, a power of attorney must still be notarized, including NW-POA-2. NW-POA-2 replaced the notarized NW-POA-1 on February 1, 2026; an NW-POA-1 signed before that date is accepted until June 30, 2026. An owner on active military deployment can use form NW-MIL-1 instead ([Selling while deployed](kb:military_deployed)). A power of attorney ends when the person who signed it dies; see [Selling a car you inherited](kb:inherited_car). Names joined by 'and' on the title need every owner; names joined by 'or' need only one.

title: Selling a car you inherited
text: If you inherited a car, you can sell it once you have the legal right to. Bring the death certificate and the court letters that name you executor or administrator of the estate (letters testamentary or letters of administration). If there are several heirs, the executor signs. A power of attorney signed by the person who died is no longer valid. If there's still a loan on the car, see [Selling a car you are still paying off](kb:selling_with_loan).

title: Selling a car you inherited
text: If you inherited a car, bring the death certificate plus one of these: court letters that name you executor or administrator of the estate, or, for a small estate that doesn't go through probate court, the heir and estate affidavit, form NW-EST-1, signed by the heir. If there are several heirs, the executor signs, or every heir signs NW-EST-1. A power of attorney ends when the person who signed it dies, so it can't be used. If there's still a loan on the car, the lender holds the title ([Selling a car you are still paying off](kb:selling_with_loan)). If the car is paid off and the title is lost, see [Selling a paid-off car when the title is lost](kb:lost_title).

title: Selling a car owned by a business
text: If the car is titled to a business, the person who signs must be authorized to sell company property. Bring the business signing authority letter, form NW-BUS-1, signed by an officer of the company, plus your photo ID and the company's tax ID number (EIN). We pay the business, not the person who signs, by direct deposit into the business bank account ([When and how you get paid](kb:getting_paid)).

title: My ex is still on the title
text: If your ex-spouse is still listed on the title, they have to sign too, the same as any co-owner ([When more than one person owns the car](kb:co_owners)). The exception: if your divorce decree awards the car to you, bring a certified copy of the decree, and your ex's signature isn't needed. If your name changed in the divorce, see [The name on the title doesn't match my ID](kb:title_name_mismatch).

title: Selling while deployed
text: If you, or a co-owner, are on active military deployment, you can sign the deployed owner authorization, form NW-MIL-1, instead of a notarized power of attorney. NW-MIL-1 is accepted in every state we serve, including Georgia, where other powers of attorney must be notarized. Sign it electronically and attach a copy of your deployment orders. The person who brings the car still needs their own photo ID ([When more than one person owns the car](kb:co_owners)).

title: Selling a family member's car for them
text: You can sell a family member's car for them if they give you a power of attorney. Ask them to sign form NW-POA-1 in front of a notary, and bring it with your own photo ID and the car's documents ([What to bring](kb:appointment_checklist)). A power of attorney ends when the person who signed it dies; if the owner has passed away, see [Selling a car you inherited](kb:inherited_car).
